title: Ruby Source Files and Code Layout
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of ruby source files and code layout in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply ruby source files and code layout in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to consistent indentation and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Ruby Source Files and Code Layout through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding ruby source files and code layout helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Ruby Source Files and Code Layout helps you reason about file extensions and execution. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: File extensions and execution. Then connect it to Newlines and statement boundaries. The remaining syllabus points—Consistent indentation—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports ruby source files and code layout. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for ruby source files and code layout using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Consistent indentation), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain ruby source files and code layout, identify its place in ruby syntax and code structure, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
